attrs.question: For retrieval-augmented generation, when does hybrid search (BM25 plus embeddings) beat pure vector search?

attrs.sub_question: What benchmark results and published evaluations (e.g., BEIR, MTEB retrieval, TREC, vendor studies from Pinecone/Weaviate/Elastic/Vespa) show hybrid BM25+dense retrieval outperforming pure dense retrieval, and under which conditions: query types (exact terms, IDs, rare entities, code, acronyms), out-of-domain or specialized corpora, low-resource languages, document length, and fusion method (RRF vs. weighted score fusion)?

What benchmark results and published evaluations (e.g., BEIR, MTEB retrieval, TREC, vendor studies from Pinecone/Weaviate/Elastic/Vespa) show hybrid BM25+dense retrieval outperforming pure dense retrieval, and under which conditions: query types (exact terms, IDs, rare entities, code, acronyms), out-of-domain or specialized corpora, low-resource languages, document length, and fusion method (RRF vs. weighted score fusion)?

When does hybrid search fail to help or actively hurt compared with pure vector search, such as with strong modern or fine-tuned embedding models, paraphrastic or semantic queries, in-domain data, poorly tuned fusion weights, or when rerankers are used, and what are its latency, complexity and cost trade-offs?
